His clothes were bloody, but he was completely healed and still floating inside the golden light.
He attempted to command the holy element to return to his body.
Still, it took a few tries with full concentration to succeed.
Unlike before, the process was swift, and the aspect entered his body in an instant.
He could feel the holy energy evenly spread across his whole body from the inside, and not a trace of mana was being felt from his own body as he swiftly landed on his feet.
An unnatural warmth tingling in his veins, skin faintly buzzing with every heartbeat, the usual inner hum of mana eerily absent, replaced by a sterile, golden glow.
This holy energy sure does hate mana.
And the same could be said for mana also, as it also tries to devour the holy energy when they collide against each other.
All the information contained inside the jade slip about the Frozen Eclipse Mana Heart Formation Technique was inside his mind.
Yet he had only gone through a part of it; he had to go through it entirely to know all the details.
But before anything, he called out status in his mind as a transparent shimmering golden screen floated in front of him.
He focused entirely on his Intelligence stat.
[Intelligence: 513]
It had triple the previous amount, which was 170.
His mind and memory felt almost unparalleled now.
He felt he had reached an entirely new dimension.
Looking at the grass, he thought he could even count the small patches just by looking, and he decided to try.
Colours seemed brighter, each blade of grass sharp and distinct.
The wind carried distant scents—damp soil, crushed leaves, the faint sweetness of wildflowers—while even the faintest rustle reached his ears as if the world itself was speaking to him.
He counted that in a 20-centimetre square on the ground, there were around 1456 blades of grass.
He did that in just a few seconds.
That was not all; he knew the range of his spatial awareness had been increased to a new degree altogether now.
And even the teleportation limit and all the other spatial-related abilities would be improved to a new degree once he practised them for a while to get used to them.

Space element was the special one, as all the elements had a massive increase in output because of his ability to control much, much more at the same time and form spells even faster, as the intelligence stat was the one most responsible for this.
Yet one thing still remained: he couldn’t even use mana now because of his holy element.
But he could see the path ahead now.

However, there was another thing he had to give focus to—the tingling sensation of his mind was being kept going for a while, which happens whenever someone messages him in the cosmic chat while tagging him.
It was as if invisible fingers tapped at the base of his skull, the sensation mingling with a faint, persistent chime only he could hear.
At first, he had thought MoonWhoEatsHerself had played a devious plan on him.
Still, he was at fault for getting into that situation.
He couldn’t blame her for that; instead, he felt he had to say thanks to her for giving him her precious technique.
Something that wasn’t being sold at the cosmic shop must be extremely valuable.
Yet, she had given it to him—her technique, which she had used herself, just like that, when they were just strangers.
It doesn’t matter if it was a kink or not; she deserved his gratitude.
He opened up the cosmic chat once, entering the same thread.
First, he decided to check back the messages which were tagging him.
MoonWhoEatsHerself:
@Elemental Paragon:My Lord, are you satisfied with the technique?
Could you please forgive me for my transgression earlier...
MoonWhoEatsHerself:
@Elemental Paragon:Lord, why aren’t you answering me?
I know I had made a big mistake, but it was only because I didn’t know who you were before.
Could you please... forgive me just this once...
I am an ignorant fool!
And a whole lot of messages in between, which are all about him forgiving her; she also used a lot of desperate and sobbing words, and it landed on her final message.
MoonWhoEatsHerself:
@Elemental Paragon:Sob..
Sob...
Please forgive me just this once.
This is getting out of hand...
To Leon, it felt like something was out of control.
It didn’t feel like a kink anymore, but more and more like she had some mental problem.
He didn’t feel great taking advantage of her, but what could he do?
He needed the technique, and the game is the game.
But it felt a bit unsettling to him.
His fingers drummed restlessly against his thigh, jaw tight with discomfort as he scrolled.
A faint chill crept up his spine, unsettled by the desperation in her words.
This is not some fantasy fairy tale but the real world.
He wasn’t going to return the jade slip because it holds too much value for him and Seraphine, as well as anyone else important to him in the future.
Still, at the very least, he would forgive her for whatever she was making up for, for a little bit of trash-talking earlier.
He couldn’t get mad at her about what she had said about his earlier.
But just then, another message came, not from her but someone else.
LimbDealer:
@Elemental Paragon: Great Lord, I didn’t know you were one of the Esteemed Lords of the Universe...
Please forgive my pathetic and dirty self for my earlier words...
Even if I get killed, please stop the others from going after my family...
I beg of you... please...
I have accepted my fate... just say that no one should touch my family...
I would be content, my Lord
You can even burn my soul for thousands of years... for me to make up for my sins...

LimbDealer, after sending his family a message to hide in different realms without any context, as he didn’t have the time, sent this message: a word from the Lord could change the fate of his family.
He had already accepted his fate, but he couldn’t let his family bear the cost of his mistake.
Reading the message from LimbDealer, Leon’s mind wobbled in shock and moved in circles and conclusions.
His brain worked like a bullet, trying to make sense of the situation.
Then the sudden realisation hit as he remembered a particular incident that happened to him in the past, which terrified him to his core.
The memory struck like an icy wave, his breath hitching, every muscle tensing as dread twisted in his gut.
It can’t be that!

chapters.title: Chapter 170: Start of Deception?
paragraphs: LimbDealer:
@Elemental Paragon: Great Lord, I didn’t know you were one of the Esteemed Lords of the Universe...
Please forgive my pathetic and dirty self for my earlier words...
Even if I get killed, please stop the others from going after my family...
I beg of you... please... I have accepted my fate... say that no one should touch my family... I would be content, my Lord.
You can even burn my soul for thousands of years... for me to make up for my sins...
After reading the message from LimbDealer.
Leon’s memory struck like an icy wave, his breath hitching, every muscle tensing as dread twisted in his gut.
It can’t be that!
He had seen those names with the title of Lord in them, which matched the class option he had had the chance to once choose from.

When he had mistakenly said the title of Lord of Space and Time, he remembered the terrifyingly weird thing that had happened around him, which made him feel dread for two whole days, thinking he had done something wrong.
His hands trembled for hours afterwards, unable to steady even when he tried to meditate. The world seemed to warp and bend at the edges of his vision.
Assume that the person named LimbDealer was referring to those Lords when he said Lord of the Universe.
But why should they think I am one of them?

He also began to understand why MoonWhoEatsHerself was acting in such a way; she might have mistaken him for a Lord of the Universe, which could be why he acquired the technique so easily. Even after that, she was still begging for her life.
The very existence of these Lords is so fearsome that even immortal beings tremble at their name. It’s hard to fathom the power they wield to instill such dread.
There was only one conclusion that came to mind, only because of what had happened in the past.
His lips parted as he said a name out loud.
Not just any name, but the name of his very own class, which he had never said out loud—slowly.
"Elemental Paragon"
Boom!

The air around him throbbed with a palpable energy, as if the very fabric of the universe was awakening in response to the name he had just spoken. It resonated with a captivating melody, akin to a celestial ringtone—a whimsical link to an expansive realm that ignited his imagination.
A sense of awe washed over him, filling his heart with both wonder and anticipation for the extraordinary journey that awaited him.
Surely, these two had experienced this by calling his name, which made them think he was a Lord of the Universe.
A wide smile couldn’t help but appear on Leon’s face, as he could already imagine what he could do while pretending to be who they thought he was—a Lord of the Universe.
Surely, he would get rich in no time when he extorted casualties from these lambs who thought he was the biggest hunter.
It was their own mistake for giving him such an opportunity; he could never pass up that, and decided to play the good guy.
Fuck that
He wouldn’t call himself evil, as it’s not like he would go as far as drinking the blood of virgins and sacrificing children just for his amusement.
Yet he was not the good guy either; he was just someone who, when an opportunity appeared, dove right into it and got the most out of it while he could.
He wasn’t sure if his cover would be blown by someone, but he still had time—he had to make big bucks.
Hehehe, this is going to be fun.

But after reading the messages from both of them, he understood one thing—they were scared shitless for their lives. Asking for his forgiveness even after that, they seemed as if they would die, especially LimbDealer, who had given up on surviving and just wanted to say that no one should touch his family.
I can’t be that cruel.
Of course, he would give his words, which seemed enough to save them, making him understand how terrifying these existences called the Lords of the Universe really were.
Not for free, of course; they are immortals—they might have big bucks stored in their causality accounts. I won’t leave anything behind.
Leon slapped his face with both hands to prepare himself and act the role of a terrifying, powerful being.
The sting jolted him, blood rushing to his cheeks. He drew a deep breath, letting the faint metallic tang at the back of his throat anchor him to the present.
Focus—don’t slip up now.
He opened up the chat once again.
What the hell
Besides the messages directly tagging him from LimbDealer and MoonWhoEatsHerself, hundreds of others were also asking for his forgiveness.
He didn’t understand why, as both of them might have insulted him, but for the others, he didn’t know what madness had gotten into them.
The messages were moving too fast; with his intelligence, he could read them, but suddenly the speed increased even more—it felt as if it had become a blur.
His eyes darted across the screen, pupils dilating as he tried to catch every word. The pressure built behind his forehead, leaving a dull ache.
If he had his mana, he would use Rajin’s Descent and Mana Body Enhancement to increase his speed to catch up, but he couldn’t do anything.

But he did read the few that were tagging him, like the ones who were begging for his forgiveness. However, others were greeting him with courtesy and praising him. Some were even messaging to tell him that his esteemed self should personally come and kill them all.
These Lords of the Universe must be very ruthless, since they are expecting him to come and kill them all.
He sent his message with just his thoughts.
Elemental Paragon:
Stop sending these words at once.
His eyes bulged out in shock as he had expected one or two to slip off, but as if the world had turned to a halt.
All the messages coming at lightning speed earlier stopped, right after he had sent his.

Fucking hell, this is too overpowered. Even the mods in the group chat in my previous world can’t do this shit; forget them—even the owner of the platform himself, if he sent a message, there would still be countless who would troll.
Especially when this thread had more than 200 thousand people in it.
And thousands of them who were active stopped just by his single command.
Seeing this, Leon smiled gleefully. He ran a hand through his hair, pulse still racing as the silence stretched. A low, breathless laugh slipped out, filling the quiet void left in the chat.
Now he never wanted his cover to be blown off; he had to be extra careful from then on.
His jaw clenched, the muscles aching beneath the skin. He rolled his shoulders back, spine straightening as if he could physically step into the role he needed to play—a sigma face.
As his following carefully thought-out message was being sent to the thousand who were holding their breath in anticipation.

chapters.title: Chapter 171: Getting Rich
paragraphs: Leon sent the following carefully thought-out message to the thousands who were holding their breath in anticipation.

A hush settled over the divine realm, the only sound the faint fwoosh of anticipation in the air. Leon could almost feel the electric prickle across his skin, as if the silence itself was holding its breath alongside the crowd, as his mind hovered over the send button.
Elemental Paragon:
I will first deal with those whose ignorance was about to cause their impending demise.

MoonWhoEatsHerself, LimbDealer felt an icy pressure pressed against the base of their throat, sending goosebumps down their spines as if a blade of pure frost hovered inches from their skin, along with hundreds of others who had mistakenly called out his name in doubt were also terrified now.
They weren’t that scared before, as punishment according to law was not True Death, just an execution and a heavy fine, which was heartbreaking in itself.

Yet for the Lord of the Universe himself to say "impending demise," they were shaken to their very cores; they were not too sure if punishment now would be something that they could walk away from with their soul intact.

News of a Lord of the Universe in Elira’s chat spread like wildfire throughout the entire divine realm, the number of people joining the chat increasing at a breakneck pace, and those who were offline were also coming online.
Notifications exploded across divine devices; servers pinged with fresh logins, and even dormant avatars flickered to life as the news rippled from thread to thread.
Flashes of multicoloured alerts strobed across screens, overlapping with a chorus of shrill notification chimes and urgent whispers echoing through every hall and chamber in the realm.
Even after joining, none of them sent a message before the Lord himself without his permission, not after he had commanded in the previous message to stop sending them.

Communication in the divine realm could be even faster than on earth itself, as now even big shots of the divine realm were also joining the chat. Still, they also dared not send their message to greet him.
They would have usually done so to show their respect, but his message had caused them to stop.
DivineEchoElira, the owner of the thread group, was also seeing everything in anticipation and excitement, as this would surely shoot her popularity to another level.
DivineEchoElira leaned closer to her display, heart pounding, already imagining the surge of followers and private messages flooding her inbox.
Like when she became famous 1000 years ago, thanks to the Lord of Space and Time drawing massive attention to her thread and sparking widespread interest in music across the divine realm.

Yet she only stayed in as a junior, spectating the event, as she knew one mishap could lead to her demise. As a Lord of the Universe, she was an absolute, but the Supremes were also to be feared in the divine realm.
Her trying something just because she had ownership of the thread would bring her only trouble.
And she could see 3 of the Supremes had currently joined the chat, and she had already made the joining message to be hidden so it wouldn’t upset the Lord.
Leon was thinking hard about what their punishment would be; he had no interest in hurting them. The only thing he wanted was a momentary gain, to earn a lot of causalties.
His gaze lingered on the glowing interface, jaw clenched as he weighed every option. The flicker of temptation in his eyes warred with a cool, calculating logic.

He still hadn’t forgotten about the item made out of him alone, put on sale by the Dimensional Keeper, a divine-ranked item. He absolutely wanted to get a hand on that item, but it would need a massive amount of causalties.
Cradle Seed of Elements (Divine– Item)
Once planted in the body, it gradually enhances all possessed elemental affinities.
Vendor: The Keeper of The Dimensions
Out of the corner of his eyes, he looked at the item in the shop.
I need a lot of causalties.
He had decided what he should do; he didn’t want to be too overbearing, which might attract the attention of other Lords.
His carefully thought-out message was sent.
Elemental Paragon:

@MoonWhoEatHerself @LimbDealer It was your ignorance that led you to this situation; however, both of you are in luck. I am not some tyrant who wants to end juniors’ lives because of their one mistake.
Your punishment is to send all the causalties you have to me as compensation. Additionally, from now on, both of you will be required to send 50% of the causalties you receive every month.
I have gotten lenient over the years; do you accept your punishment?
And none shall touch you or anyone related to you, as you have to live to bear the weight of your sins.
MoonWhoEatHerself and LimbDealer cried and sobbed in their places; one in her room, the other in his office.
MoonWhoEatHerself’s shoulders sagged with relief, tears smudging her digital avatar. LimbDealer released a shaky breath, hands trembling over the shimmering screen, unable to believe their reprieve.
This punishment seemed like nothing compared to what could have happened to them. One thought formed in their minds:
Lord Elemental Paragon is really kind.

They hurriedly sent their replies, wiping away the tears of joy. This would make their life harder, but not too much. Also, the Lord had only asked for 50%, which showed he didn’t want them to stagnate their future potential, as resources are one of the most important things to go forward.
They had to work much harder now, but they would do their best and never forget this generosity.

Leon was holding his breath in anticipation, as he felt he had done too much, having taken all their current causalties and going as far as taking 50% of the causalties they earn in their immortal life from now on.
He trusted his intuition; they were so fearful and awed by his presence that he decided to assert himself properly, all while giving them room to breathe.
He held his breath in anticipation—would he get the lifetime cash cow or not?
And then a message came.
@MoonWhoEatHerself:
My Lord, you have my heartfelt gratitude for giving us a chance. I will happily accept every term of yours.
@LimbDealer:
Great, thank you for sparing me and the doom that would have come to my family. Even if it feels a little, I would send 80% of my monthly causalties earned.
I am just too grateful that I can live with my family; you have my heartfelt gratitude.

LimbDealer, a guildmaster of a small-sized guild in the divine realm with a business of monster parts around the divine realm, which was still in development, didn’t feel a single bit of regret when he had increased his own monthly compensation.

Unlike MoonWhoEatHerself, who doesn’t seem to have a family like nearly 75% of the immortals, he had a lovely family; he felt it was only right to show his gratefulness to the Lord, as he was also not a poor man, and could be considered a wealthy immortal.
Leon, reading the message of both of them, bit his lips, especially after the message of LimbDealer.
A faint taste of copper grounded him as regret and satisfaction warred in his chest."
He felt like he had gone too easy on them.
There was a bit of regret, but he also felt his conditions were quite fair.
He knew he couldn’t change his words now; they saw him as a Lord of the Universe, and he couldn’t shoot himself in the foot by taking his own words back now.
Suddenly, two messages from the system in the form of shimmering golden pop-ups appeared in front of him.
A sharp chiming sound rang out in his mind, accompanied by a golden flash that painted the air in shimmering light, making Leon’s pupils contract reflexively.
Seeing the messages, Leon’s little bit of regret washed away like it was not even there to begin with.
"kek kek, I am going to be rich soon"

Leon was holding his breath in anticipation, as he felt he had done too much, having taken all their current causalties and going as far as taking 50% of the causalties they earn in their immortal life from now on.
He trusted his intuition; they were so fearful and awed by his presence that he decided to assert himself properly, all while giving them room to breathe.
He held his breath in anticipation—would he get the lifetime cash cow or not?
And then a message came.
@MoonWhoEatHerself:
My Lord, you have my heartfelt gratitude for giving us a chance.
I will happily accept every term of yours.
@LimbDealer:
Great, thank you for sparing me and the doom that would have come to my family.
Even if it feels a little, I would send 80% of my monthly causalties earned.
I am just too grateful that I can live with my family; you have my heartfelt gratitude.

LimbDealer, a guildmaster of a small-sized guild in the divine realm with a business of monster parts around the divine realm, which was still in development, didn’t feel a single bit of regret when he had increased his own monthly compensation.

Unlike MoonWhoEatHerself, who doesn’t seem to have a family like nearly 75% of the immortals, he had a lovely family; he felt it was only right to show his gratefulness to the Lord, as he was also not a poor man, and could be considered a wealthy immortal.
Leon, reading the message of both of them, bit his lips, especially after the message of LimbDealer.
A faint taste of copper grounded him as regret and satisfaction warred in his chest."
He felt like he had gone too easy on them.
There was a bit of regret, but he also felt his conditions were quite fair.
He knew he couldn’t change his words now; they saw him as a Lord of the Universe, and he couldn’t shoot himself in the foot by taking his own words back now.
Suddenly, two messages from the system in the form of shimmering golden pop-ups appeared in front of him.
A sharp chiming sound rang out in his mind, accompanied by a golden flash that painted the air in shimmering light, making Leon’s pupils contract reflexively.
Seeing the messages, Leon’s little bit of regret washed away like it was not even there to begin with.
"kek kek, I am going to be rich soon"

chapters.title: Chapter 172: Dread or Rich
paragraphs: [MoonWhoEatHerself was trying to send you 1.2 million causalties]
[Do you accept]
[yes]
[No]
Without thinking about anything, with a broad smile etched on his face, Leon quickly accepted the causalties transfer.
His fingers tingled with anticipation as he clicked the option, the faint electric hum of the system brushing against his skin.
heheh I had to rob an entire kingdom to get 600k causalties and now in one go without doing much I got 1.2 million
[1.2 million causalties had been added to your account]
Then another message came, which made his eyes bulge in excitement and shock.
[LimbDealer was trying to send you 6.7 million causalties]
[Do you accept]
[yes]
[No]
Fucking hell, LimbDealer sure is rich
Leon didn’t feel anything wrong with these numbers. He had experienced firsthand how the value of causality changes for the same platinum bar, so they should be adjusted to the realms.
Otherwise, the 790 million price for the divine item would be too cheap.
He accepted the causalties once again with a broad smile on his face while rubbing his hands.
[6.7 million causalties had been added to your account]
Seeing the message, he couldn’t help but his body shook in joy.
A tremor of exhilaration ran down his spine, his shoulders twitching with laughter he barely managed to contain.
The air seemed to vibrate with his excitement, the taste of triumph almost sweet on his tongue.
"7.9 million causalties in such a short time, it won’t be long before I get my hands on the divine treasure worth 790 million"
He had already collected more than 1% percent of the total.
Leon’s palms warmed as he rubbed them together, unable to suppress the childlike giddiness bubbling beneath his calm facade.
And he was still not done yet.
He didn’t even know what other hundreds of people had done wrong, but he didn’t care. He just had to give his punishment and get the fairkekcompensation he deserves.
He just had to act it out.
Elemental Paragon:
@MoonWhoEatHerself and @LimbDealer, you have been given your chance. It will be up to you how you follow it through to the end or not. I am merciful, but that doesn’t mean I give another chance.
Your Fate lies in your own hands now.
MoonWhoEatHerself:
My Lord, I will not disappoint you

She knew those 1.2 million causalties might not be much to him, but it was only due to his kindness that she had survived today; she could never ever think of failing to fulfil his kind demands. She might forget her own name, but never the price she had to pay for her sins.
LimbDealer:
I will never forget your generosity, my Lord.
Leon looked at their responses, his brow furrowed, lips parting as he searched for logic in their reverent replies, unable to grasp the depth of their fear.
He had understood they were too terrified of Lords and him, the one they thought was a Lord also, but didn’t understand what these Lords had done to make them act like such docile creatures.
They are all immortal beings, likely similar to a God in his current world.
Who cares, I just had to fill my pocket nicely.
Asking for such a thing would definitely bring suspicion to him, so Leon doesn’t care at all.
Elemental Paragon:
Good
Now he moved on to those hundreds of others who, for some reason, were also begging for his forgiveness earlier.
Fuck I don’t know what they are guilty of to begin with!
But surely I won’t be as bad as these two, who had directly disrespected me because of their ignorance.
He would be shooting his shot in the air; he just hoped no one would be suspicious of him.
I have to sound confident and overbearing.
Taking a deep breath and having a few moments of thought, Leon finally decided on their punishment also.
He had no interest in harming; he just wanted causality, the more the better, but he couldn’t go too hard this time.
Whatever they had done couldn’t be equal to those before.
Elemental Paragon:
For those who have also made mistakes, please submit 25% of your current causalties to me. You must also submit 25% of the monthly casualty earned forever.
Do you accept your punishment?

After sending the message, Leon held his breath in fear and anticipation. There were hundreds of them now. What if someone disrespected him directly or, in the worst case, challenged him? From what he had seen, it would likely not happen.
But who knew, some psycho might be present in here.
A bead of sweat trickled down his temple, and the silence seemed to press in on his ears, heavy and suffocating.

The six other Supremes of the Divine realms, who were currently observing the exchange, felt that this Lord was quite humble. He even gave these lowly pests a chance to accept; a formality on his part, but it only underscored his humility.

Even the punishment given by him seemed to them like a light slap, their memory still sharp with the day when the whole planet was frozen in time and space with thousands of Lesser Divinity, hundreds of Greater Divinity, along with a few Prime Divinity like them.
The memory of icy, suffocating stillness clawed at their minds—the world suspended in eerie silence, every breath crystallising in reality.
Especially, they can never forget the actual death of Supreme like them, not any Prime Divinity.
And the millions and millions of other humans inside the planet, she didn’t even care. She froze everything in her masterful brilliance of time and space without even blinking twice.
Lord Elemental Paragon seemed too generous and kind.

But one thing they did understand from this exchange—this Lord sure loves causalties quite a lot, they can’t understand his thinking as causality can only do so much, yet knowing this, all of them think there had to be something, even a Lord showing interest in them.

Or it could be that it was used as a means to make them feel punished. Either way, even for the tiniest bit of possibility, their interest in researching those causalities which no one even cared about arose now, because of the new Lord Elemental Paragon, they think they might find some secrets about them, if they understood them well.
Besides the current understanding they have of them.
Leon’s worry was unjustifiable as he could now only see the golden screen blur past, with messages like "Thank you for your generosity", "I am forever grateful", like them.
That wasn’t just with their messages. Along with them, hundreds of notifications from the system were popping up in front of him.
His vision blurred under the barrage of golden flashes, the sharp chime of each alert stinging his ears like melodies.
"Hahahahaha!!"
This made Leon burst into laughter, his whole body brimming with joy.
Laughter erupted from his chest, raw and unrestrained, his hands clenched together as his body shook with glee.
As in one go, with just his thought, he accepted all the gifts they were giving him.
[A Total of 187.5 million causalties had been added to your account.]
Seeing the number, another full-blown laughter couldn’t help but burst out of him.
"Hahahaha, I am rich! kek kek"
But his laughter was cut short, and a feeling of dread washed over his entire body down to his single cells.
It was replaced by a cold weight settling in his gut. A chill prickled up his arms as the new message seared across his vision.
[Lord of Illusion and Mystery had joined the chat.]
A sudden, icy draft swept through the air, raising goosebumps across his skin. His pulse slowed, as if time itself had thickened.

chapters.title: Chapter 173: Unexpected turns?
paragraphs: Leon stood alone at the edge of the field, the tall grass whispering at his ankles.
[Lord of Illusion and Mystery has joined the chat.]
A sudden, icy draft swept through the air, raising goosebumps across his skin. His pulse slowed, as if time itself had thickened.
W-What? Lord of Illusion and Mystery—shit!
Shit! Shit!
Don’t panic. I have to act calm and keep up my act. No one will know anything.
He knew his identity and location were protected by the mysterious cosmic system.
His hands fumbled with the edge of his robe, knuckles white, legs bouncing in place as he struggled to stay still.
Just act cool
He just had to act cool, and nothing would happen.
If she decides to talk to me, I’ll not answer... or give vague replies.
He suspected her reason for appearing might be him—someone claiming to be a Lord, just like her.
Which meant she came for him.
Lord of Illusion and Mystery:"Who are you, Elemental Paragon?"
Seeing her message, Leon couldn’t just ignore it. His future career as a causality farmer might be in danger if she suspected he was an imposter.
He felt a bead of sweat slip down his temple, heartbeat drumming so loud he thought she might hear it.
He had to play the role of a mysterious master who had been in seclusion for a very long time.
It was not a choice but a necessity for him.
Elemental Paragon:"Why should I tell you, Lord of Illusion and Mystery?"
The woman with otherworldly beauty and an excited look on her face stared at the golden shimmering screen with growing intrigue.
Lord of Illusion and Mystery:"Fair enough."
Lord of Illusion and Mystery:"But I’ve never heard of you before. Where did you come from?"
Leon didn’t overthink and answered again.
Elemental Paragon:"Why should I tell you, Lord of Illusion and Mystery?"
She—whose title literally contained the word "Mystery"—grew even more excited.
Her fingers traced the transparent chat screen, a predatory smile tugging at her lips.
People usually acted bland in front of her, except for her only cute and lovely Nys.
But now she had found a mysterious toy.
Lord of Illusion and Mystery:"Hehe... I like mysteries quite a lot, dear Elemental Paragon. So you don’t have to tell me anything."
"But I do have an offer for you. You have to answer one question, and I can give you 100 million casualties for that.
"What do you think? You seem to like them. You must have just become a Lord or..."
"Then again, it’s still a mystery to me what use you could have for them. They’re just worthless to us Lords..."
A pause, and she continued.
"You’re very interesting, Elemental Paragon."
Even for a Lord like her, 100 million was a decent amount of causality.
Leon, hearing her words, had stars in his eyes.
His breath caught in his throat, eyes wide. He nearly laughed out loud in glee.

Just answering one question would get him 100 million casualties? He could never give up on that. He needed to collect the cradle seeds of elements, which cost 790 million casualties. He would never have enough.
It’s not like I have to answer if she asks something too complicated. I can dodge the question. I can’t pass up this easy opportunity to earn some extra money.
As for her other strange assumptions about him, he decided not to comment. Let her imagination run wild all she wanted.
Elemental Paragon:"I would answer your question, but it will depend on what you ask of me."
Lord of Illusion and Mysterysmiled faintly at his reply. If he had accepted too easily, she would’ve found it dull.
Lord of Illusion and Mystery:"Now answer me, Elemental Paragon—are you from the same universe as us or not?"
That was all she wanted to know. If he were from a different universe altogether, she would never be able to find him due to the Universal Wall surrounding their own.
She didn’t understand how he had gained access to their cosmic chatroom—this had never happened before.
They didn’t know what lay beyond the walls, but many Lords had similar theories.

And if another Lord had truly been born in their universe, the universal phenomenon triggered at such times wouldn’t have gone unnoticed. So she was sure—something about Elemental Paragon was truly mysterious.
Even his name, when spoken, had triggered the cosmic phenomenon, which only occurred when someone reached their realm.
Leon heard her question.
She’s asking if I’m from the same universe as her... I have literally no clue.

But it is a big deal to her. My earlier plan to act as a secluded master might have flopped. She already has her own theories about my identity. I don’t know how much knowledge she has, but I’ll play along and string her along her own path.

He was reasonably sure he was currently in the same universe as her—but what about Earth? What realm would that be considered? Did Earth even exist in the same universe to begin with? It had no magic at all.
He had no answer to that question.
He chewed at his lower lip, brow knitting as uncertainty twisted in his gut.
I’m technically from Earth—my previous world—and this new one too.
So for one, he was a bit sure that he and the Lord were in the same universe—but the other Earth, he wasn’t so confident.

He didn’t want to lie. No matter what, she was a Lord of the Universe—an existence even divinities trembled before. Lin Fang, the genius dark elf he’d mentioned before—those were just ants before beings like her.
He didn’t want to deceive her and risk saying something that might backfire in the future.
Practically, his soul was from Earth. Maybe he was from both universes—if they were different.
Elemental Paragon:"I’m actually not sure."
Up until now, the Lord of Illusion and Mystery had been calm in her dimension. But seeing that reply, even she was a bit perplexed now as her eyes turned sharp.
A glowing, white-purplish ring formed around her colourless eyes—no pupils—just a rotating circular glow. It spun faster as her focus sharpened.
Strange white and purplish mist formed around her body. After a second, it vanished, and the glow faded back into her skin.
He’s telling the truth.
The mystery around Elemental Paragon ran deeper than she had thought.

Lord of Illusion and Mystery:"Don’t worry, my dear mysterious new Lord. I will find where you live... who you are... what your real name is... where you came from... where you were born... how you look..."
It continued. And continued. Her words turned more intense, more chilling, until a cold shiver crept up Leon’s spine. He couldn’t help but tremble in fear.
Lord of Illusion and Mystery:"Just wait for me, dear Elemental Paragon. This Lord will be paying you a visit soon. And we’ll continue our chat... from there."
[Lord of Illusion and Mystery has left the chat.]
The silence pressed in, so heavy it felt like a physical weight on his chest. Every breath burned a little colder.
He could only stand there frozen in place, shaking. Her last message had terrified him completely.

The golden chat screen faded, and Leon was left alone in the silence of the field. The sky overhead seemed a little darker, the wind colder than before. His legs threatened to give out, and he wrapped his arms around himself, shivering. The scent of crushed grass and damp Earth filled his nose. Leon’s heartbeat pounded in his ears, the echo of fear still burning in his veins.
A literal Lord of the Universe was now coming after him.
Fuck my shitty luck!Along with the thought, another notification, which he ignored, because his thoughts were filled with dread of his future.
For a moment, he almost convinced himself it was just an empty threat—until his legs gave way, and he sank to the ground, breath short and ragged.

The scent of crushed grass and damp Earth filled his nose.
Leon’s heartbeat pounded in his ears, the echo of fear still burning in his veins.
A literal Lord of the Universe was now coming after him.
Fuck my shitty luck!Along with the thought, another notification, which he ignored, because his thoughts were filled with dread of his future.
For a moment, he almost convinced himself it was just an empty threat—until his legs gave way, and he sank to the ground, breath short and ragged.

chapters.title: Chapter 174: Rich—Buying an Item
paragraphs: For a moment, he almost convinced himself it was just an empty threat—until his legs gave way, and he sank to the ground, breath short and ragged.
The chill of the grass pressed against his palms, the damp earth seeping through his fingers as he steadied himself, a faint tremor running up his arms.
Finally, after a while, Leon calmed his nerves and stood up in his spot. His breathing was still heavy, knowing a Lord of the Universe was trying to hunt him down.
A cold bead of sweat traced down his temple, mingling with the humid air, as the distant hum of wind rustled the blades of grass around his feet.
He sent his last message in the ongoing Chat.
[Elemental Paragon had left the Chat]
While those who at least wanted to greet the Lord of the Universe were flabbergasted as even another Lord came and had some strange conversation, after that, both of them left quickly.
[Lord of Illusion and Mystery is trying to send you 100 million Causality]
[Attached message: I will find you soon~]
Leon quickly accepted the Causality to make the creepy message disappear in front of him.
Taking a few deep breaths, he sat on the grassy ground. He was about to delve more into theFrozen Eclipse Mana Heart Formation Techniqueso he could deal with the holy energy.
[Moon Celestial is trying to send you 10 million Causality along with an item.]

[Attached message: I am the guild master of the MoonWhoEatHerself. This is an official token of appreciation from our Guild Lord Elemental Paragon for forgiving the junior and our guild. Please accept it.]
He accepted the casualties and items with just a thought; he was curious to see what item the guild master of the White Moon guild had sent.
Another 10 million casualties had been added to his account, and a rectangular-shaped white box with bluish, golden engraving on it appeared by the glitch in reality.
He caught it gently with his hand and opened the box right away with curiosity.
And it revealed a white jade with a strange ancient pattern on it, which looked much more complex than the previous jade, which was green in colour and had different patterns on it.
Just by touching the jade in his hand, he felt as if he was being bathed in pure moonlight, pleasant and relaxing.
Is this another technique for mana heart formation? This one has a heaven-and-earth difference from the previous one.
His thoughts weren’t even finished when another notification from the system popped up in front of him in the form of a shimmering golden transparent screen.
[Sword Supreme is trying to send you 20 million Causality along with an item.]

[Attached message: I am the leader of a small guild named Heavenly Swords. Accept this as a token of gratitude for sparing the younger generation of the Divine Realm, and you are always welcome in our Celestial Sword constellation.]
Leon accepted the free causalities with a smile on his face; he can never give up on his act of being Lord of the Universe now, as it was too profitable.
A new box appeared out of the glitch in reality, but this time it was not rectangular-shaped but shaped like a sword.
It was black in colour with golden engraving all across the box, as if it was creating a strange sense of harmony.
When he held the box, his finger traced its smooth texture, but there was also a conflicting, sharp sensation—almost like gripping the sharpened edge of a blade with bare hands.
He opened the box, and it revealed a black jade with ancient patterns on it in the form of a sword.
He thought it was done, but for 30 minutes straight, message after message came back-to-back from different beings.
His vision blurred for a moment under the endless barrage of shimmering notifications, each new alert sending a soft, crystallinedingthat echoed through the quiet glade.

17 of which he had remembered the names of, including the Sword Supreme, as those with the title supreme attached to them, none of them had gifted less than 20 million Causality, and one even sent his freaking 50 million Causality along with the jade slip like others.
11 were supremes, and 6 others were also with noteworthy gifts, and their techniques also seemed to match the level of Sword Supreme.
Other than these big shots, there were countless others, too, who donated from the 3 million to the 10 million range.
But one thing was that the technique sent by the White Moon guild also matches the Aura emanating from the method given to him by the Supremes.
Besides their modest donation, their technique was of a very high level.
In total, after he had left the cosmic Chat, he had gained freaking 713 million casualties.
His heart was beating too loudly, knowing how many casualties he had just achieved by this exchange alone.
He opens his system and heads directly to the shop, where he checks the corner of the transparent screen to see the balance of his causalities.
His fingers hovered mid-air, heart pounding in his chest, the faint golden glow of the interface illuminating his wide-eyed expression.
[Causality: 1009000000]
He had a feeling in his heart, but still counted the total digits in his balance.
One.. two... five... Ten
"O-One billion n-ninety million freaking casualties"
"Dear Gods!!"
A surge of dizzy exhilaration left his knees weak, his breath catching in his throat, as the enormity of the numbers finally sank in.
He had expected to earn a couple of hundred million when he had seen the amount sent by MoonWhoEatHerself, but this was entirely out of his expectations.
He had become a billionaire in this incident, where he had acted as a fraudulent Lord of the Universe.
I’d better keep this secret to my grave, or else even my soul wouldn’t be able to rest even after my death, if I am caught.
I can even buy the only divine-ranked item in the whole cosmic shop now

It only costs around 790 million. Even after that, he would have a lot of casualties left. After buying the cradle of elemental seed, he had another item in his eyes, which he was sure he was going to buy next, not for himself but for someone else.
Who could it be?
Yes, it was none other than Seraphine.
26. Seed of Stormlight Heart(Mythical – Item)
Implants within the user evolve their lightning and light affinities over time.
Vendor:Lord of Lightning and Luminance
It was the seed of Stormlight Heart, which he thinks would suit Seraphine perfectly; he didn’t understand why these lords were selling such a good item and were not using it on themselves.
The only conclusion he got was that these treasures might not be of any use to them.
He doesn’t know how high their affinities might be; that mythical rank would have no effect on the Lord of Lightning and Luminance, who had the same affinity as the treasure.

It doesn’t matter to him, but he just hopes this treasure will increase Seraphine’s affinity to a new degree over time. Still, his only worry was whether she would be able to use the treasure or not, as it had light affinity.
I will worry about that later, and I will make it work somehow
He scrolled down the shop and, without even blinking, bought an item worth 2.5 million casualties.
A wide smile on his face as he saw it materialise in front of him.

chapters.title: Chapter 175: Lifeline—Ready!
paragraphs: Leon gazed at the item, a faint sigh of relief passing over his face, and purchased it without hesitation.
Phoenix Feather Amulet (Legendary – Item)
Revives the wearer upon death, once.
Vendor:Resurrecto Maximus

A transparent, square-shaped glass materialized in front of him, emerging from a glitch in reality. Inside, a single feather was draped in golden-crimson fire, its flames swirling but never consuming the vibrant crimson feather. The feather bore a sun symbol near the bottom, close to its golden tip, where a fine line stretched through the center. The glass refracted light at impossible angles, scattering fragmented rainbow patterns across the floor.

Leon took the glass container holding the Phoenix Feather Amulet in his hand, surprised by the sensation—a gentle, almost contradictory cold warmth radiated from the surface. He had expected the glass to be searing hot, but instead, only a faint, nearly imperceptible warmth prickled at his skin.

He opened the case. Instantly, the heat intensified tenfold, but still, it did not burn him. Instead, he felt an odd, cool heat emanating from the feather itself. Any ordinary person would likely have been scorched, but Leon, with his rank 7 Fire affinity, remained unaffected.
As the lid opened, a strange voice echoed in his mind, the tone rasping, as if whispered through a closed door, with a cold, grating laughter at the end.
Drop your blood on the feather and keep it close to your body. If not, you won’t even get the chance to complain about the feather. Kek kek!
Leon understood the message, but that laugh—worse than James’s—had to be an achievement in itself.
A dagger appeared in his hand from his inventory.Fwoosh.With a small cut to his finger—shink—the blade drew a bead of crimson, which dropped onto the Phoenix feather.
He did not flinch.
As his blood touched the golden-crimson fire, the flame swallowed the drop, merging it into the feather until it vanished completely.
The feather in his hand remained warm, yet now he sensed a profound connection to it as if it stood ready to defend him and send him a message.
Drop dead and I’ll just hit "respawn."
The message had told him to keep the feather close. His inventory, directly linked to his soul, was the closest place possible, so he tried storing it there.
But the moment it entered his inventory, that connection disappeared.
Hmm, that won’t work; I have to keep it physically close to me.

He took out a string crafted from the best material he could find within his inventory. Stretching the cord with force, he found it brittle—the fibers creaked, then snapped with a softcrack. It failed immediately.
"Useless," he muttered, watching the brittle fibers scatter.If I use this, even strong winds might take my precious lifeline away
He needed something far better.

With a thought, Leon opened his cosmic shop and browsed the selection of monster parts. He quickly found monster spider silk, ranked epic, for 10,000 causality. Cheaper options existed, but he had no intention of cutting corners—not after spending 2.5 million causality on the Phoenix Feather.

The spider silk appeared in his hand. Unlike a thin web, it was a solid strand, gleaming white with a metallic luster. The silk was smooth, unexpectedly heavy, with a texture reminiscent of woven steel. He only needed a small length, but the coil in his hand measured over ten meters. He tried to break it with his strength, but the silk did not yield. Even at his strongest, he doubted he could snap it.
Whatever monster this came from must have been formidable.

He summoned his blade of convenient sharpness. Unsheathing it, he sliced through the silk.Snick.The blade parted the strand effortlessly, as if slicing tofu. He had braced for resistance, but there was none.

A satisfied grin tugged at his lips; even the blade seemed pleased. Both items were epic ranked, yet the blade cut through the silk with absurd ease, confirming his suspicions about the weapon’s unusual nature.

He stored the rest of the spider silk and the scattered techniques littering the ground, selecting only a few to study for the formation of his mana heart. Time pressed on him; he had just over four years to solve his problem and refused to risk himself in a weakened state.
There was another path—practicing the holy element, now that it was no longer repulsive. Still, he hesitated; he didn’t want to rely on it yet. He wanted to conquer it on his own terms.
Abandoning his mana or affinities was unthinkable, especially since he had no idea what his strength would become if he did. He aimed to harness holy energy along with every affinity at his disposal.

The holy energy’s tremendous power and healing properties were vital—while not as fast as his life affinity, it was essential for shielding his mind. He knew well how devastating mental attacks could be, and holy energy would cover that vulnerability. He refused to give up anything and intended to have it all.
He clenched his fists, knuckles whitening with determination.

The Phoenix Feather Amulet now hung from his chest. Leon sat cross-legged in meditation, wearing a fresh outfit in place of the one soaked with blood. His hair and face were washed clean—he had used water from his emergency supply, since his mana was still sealed. The experience only deepened his appreciation for the elements he wielded.

Once more, he formed a protective pillar of golden holy energy around himself. Then, he drew out the white jade from the box given by the Moon Celestial. Nineteen other boxes, each with its own unique mark, lay scattered around him.

He held the white jade, instantly soothed by its tranquil, moonlit energy. Without mana, he poured holy energy into the jade, attempting to connect. It took sixteen attempts before the energy was finally accepted—the jade had resisted, even within the golden pillar, as if allergic to it.
Now, the white jade slip hovered before him, humming with intensity—a sign that he had succeeded.
Leon’s expression hardened with resolve. What was coming next would be on a completely different level from any technique he’d faced before.

chapters.title: Chapter 176: Mana Character
paragraphs: Leon was ready.
Or at least, that’s what he kept telling himself. As if anyone’s ever really "ready" for getting their brain scrambled like eggs.
Famous last words.
It struck his mind like a brutal attack, even though it was supposed to be information to help him learn a new technique.
"Arrrggghhh!"

Stabbing agony lanced through his temples, heat prickling across his scalp as each pulse throbbed behind his eyes. Thump, thump, thump—his heart hammered against his ribs. A metallic tang coated his tongue, sharper than blood alone. Cold sweat dripped down his spine, pooling beneath him on the grass, the sweet scent of crushed wildflowers mixing with the coppery air.
His mind grew hazy, the world spun around him, and the last thing he remembered was the white jade slip humming in front of him.
He lost consciousness.
His brain took damage from the overload of information, as cobweb-like tears appeared within.

When the holy energy surged, it brought not just warmth—he felt it seep through every nerve, like cool water poured over a burn, the pain receding in soothing, slow waves. Hiss... The ringing in his ears dulled.
He was unconscious for only 30 seconds.
[Intelligence +12]
Shit, I didn’t know—even after all the previous torture—I would still lose consciousness on the first hit, all that gritting my teeth and gaining enlightenment for nothing.

This was the first and only time he was knocked out by the mental shock of information. Afterward, he only reached the brink of haziness but never lost consciousness again and was able to form his thoughts.
His body stayed tense throughout, and although he didn’t lose his mind again, the pain remained intense.

The whole process lasted for half an hour. During the first fifteen minutes, his cry of pain traveled across the grassy plain, mingling with the constant healing of both his mind and body, which made him euphoric.
For the last few minutes, he wore a serene expression, as a slight tinge of pain was nothing compared to the comfort of being enveloped in holy energy.
After he finished with the first jade, it dropped to the ground like any ordinary stone; all the information about the Celestial White Moon Mana Heart Transformation was now in his mind.
He just had to look through it to fully understand.
Alright, enough stalling. Time to go fry my brain some more.
He didn’t stop there and focused on the other nineteen techniques he had chosen, scattered explicitly around him.
His intelligence stat had increased once more.
He didn’t even check the stat and moved directly to the following technique.
While he could have tried to understand the Celestial White Moon Mana Heart Transformation first and then continued—which would have made it easier for his mind—he did not.
He intentionally chose not to, as this was not just about learning various techniques from which he could deduce how to form his mana heart using holy energy.
There was another big opportunity in front of him.
The intelligence stat.
A combination of holy energy and these high-level techniques, which were packed with too much information, was the perfect fuel for his intelligence stat.
The process of absorbing different techniques continued as time passed quickly.

Twelve hours straight had passed; he had learned all the techniques, and his intelligence stat had increased to a new level. His brain was filled with so much information that he was barely able to contain it.
Leon felt exhausted; his mind and body both tired, his eyes droopy, and he could have fallen asleep at any moment.
But after preparing bedding for himself, he called out his stats in his mind before taking a peaceful, long sleep.
His focus was only on one thing.
[Intelligence: 805]
He saw a massive jump in his intelligence.
It was all worth the torture, he thought, a smile tugging at his lips as he lay comfortably on the soft mattress and fell into a deep slumber as soon as his body touched the softness.
In the same endless expanse of grassy field.
No sunlight was there to wake him, yet he woke up on his own, rubbing his eyelids and stretching his arms. Leon finally felt refreshed.
He didn’t know how long he had slept, but it was all worth it; he needed the rest.

He took out the cutlery, along with a steaming hot steak, soft, fluffy bread, a dish made from his potato and other ingredients, and some red wine, which didn’t make him feel drunk, but he still enjoyed the flavor.
He took each bite leisurely and savored every flavor.
Mmmh, so good!
If only enlightenment tasted half as good as steak.

He felt much more relaxed now. He could see the path ahead, and the tension in his mind had lessened quite a bit. This lunch, dinner, or breakfast—whatever it was—felt much more savory than before, even though it was the same food.
Yet it tasted different.
Storing everything inside his inventory with just a thought—fwoosh—as it all vanished.
He assumed a meditating position on the ground, his expression resolute as he began to study the first technique, Celestial White Moon Mana Formation Techniques.
As he processed the information, he started to understand why these techniques contained such a large amount of knowledge.
In addition to forming the mana heart, the technique explained how it was created.
Moon affinity was not an affinity in itself, but derived from the combination of different affinities.
Elements like
Water
Ice
Shadow
Illusion
And lastly, time.
These elements made up the core of Moon Affinity.
Five affinities for one power? Who designed this system, a committee?
But water, the most basic affinity, took up the most significant part, reaching 45% of Moon Affinity.
Then ice: 20%.
Shadow: 15%.
Illusion: 15%.
Time: 5%.
This was the combination the founder of the Celestial White Moon Technique used to create her unique Moon affinity.
A blend of various affinities to make a unique one of her own.
The idea itself blew Leon’s mind completely away.
The founder’s words stated her technique was not perfect—no method was—as the limitation of affinity was always there, based on the five affinities she had and factoring in the rank of each one.
A harmony of balance between the affinities was the accumulation of her entire life.
An affinity of her own, which formed a single affinity that surpassed every affinity she had, breaking the power barrier imposed by affinity rank.
Other than her rank 7 water affinity, the others were mediocre, with her time affinity reaching only rank 1.
Practically unusable to her, she still managed to make it work and create a new affinity.
Leon felt goosebumps at the dedication and time she put into creating an entirely new affinity, breaking through the rank barrier.
He didn’t know her, yet he respected her. Reading this text so easily felt like cheating.

Other alternative methods were also mentioned, some needing only two affinities, which she learned along her journey. She said they were just weak imitations of her perfect moon affinity, consisting of all the affinities she had and never outclassing hers.
To learn the technique, at least two affinities were needed.

After the process of learning to create Moon Affinity was done, there came the long, arduous task of using Moon Mana as a strand to weave your own heart and a complex rune inside, which supports the whole heart and gives it life.
It was stated that, depending on the person, it could take as long as one hundred years to form their mana heart, or as little as one year; everything depended on the one who was creating it.

Leon’s expression was solemn after learning everything, as he couldn’t use his affinities at all. How was he supposed to create Moon Affinity in the first place—let alone form the mana heart? Yet as the realization settled in, a cold weight pressed into his chest. He stared into the void, wondering if this was where his journey would finally halt.
And here I thought I was the main character.

sentences.text: Leon was ready.
Or at least, that’s what he kept telling himself.
As if anyone’s ever really "ready" for getting their brain scrambled like eggs.
Famous last words.
It struck his mind like a brutal attack, even though it was supposed to be information to help him learn a new technique.
"Arrrggghhh!"
Stabbing agony lanced through his temples, heat prickling across his scalp as each pulse throbbed behind his eyes.
Thump, thump, thump—his heart hammered against his ribs.
A metallic tang coated his tongue, sharper than blood alone.
Cold sweat dripped down his spine, pooling beneath him on the grass, the sweet scent of crushed wildflowers mixing with the coppery air.
His mind grew hazy, the world spun around him, and the last thing he remembered was the white jade slip humming in front of him.
He lost consciousness.
His brain took damage from the overload of information, as cobweb-like tears appeared within.
When the holy energy surged, it brought not just warmth—he felt it seep through every nerve, like cool water poured over a burn, the pain receding in soothing, slow waves.
Hiss...
The ringing in his ears dulled.
He was unconscious for only 30 seconds.
[Intelligence +12]
Shit, I didn’t know—even after all the previous torture—I would still lose consciousness on the first hit, all that gritting my teeth and gaining enlightenment for nothing.
This was the first and only time he was knocked out by the mental shock of information.
Afterward, he only reached the brink of haziness but never lost consciousness again and was able to form his thoughts.
His body stayed tense throughout, and although he didn’t lose his mind again, the pain remained intense.
The whole process lasted for half an hour.
During the first fifteen minutes, his cry of pain traveled across the grassy plain, mingling with the constant healing of both his mind and body, which made him euphoric.
For the last few minutes, he wore a serene expression, as a slight tinge of pain was nothing compared to the comfort of being enveloped in holy energy.
After he finished with the first jade, it dropped to the ground like any ordinary stone; all the information about the Celestial White Moon Mana Heart Transformation was now in his mind.
He just had to look through it to fully understand.
Alright, enough stalling.
Time to go fry my brain some more.
He didn’t stop there and focused on the other nineteen techniques he had chosen, scattered explicitly around him.
His intelligence stat had increased once more.
He didn’t even check the stat and moved directly to the following technique.
While he could have tried to understand the Celestial White Moon Mana Heart Transformation first and then continued—which would have made it easier for his mind—he did not.
He intentionally chose not to, as this was not just about learning various techniques from which he could deduce how to form his mana heart using holy energy.
There was another big opportunity in front of him.
The intelligence stat.
A combination of holy energy and these high-level techniques, which were packed with too much information, was the perfect fuel for his intelligence stat.
The process of absorbing different techniques continued as time passed quickly.
Twelve hours straight had passed; he had learned all the techniques, and his intelligence stat had increased to a new level.
His brain was filled with so much information that he was barely able to contain it.
Leon felt exhausted; his mind and body both tired, his eyes droopy, and he could have fallen asleep at any moment.
But after preparing bedding for himself, he called out his stats in his mind before taking a peaceful, long sleep.
His focus was only on one thing.
[Intelligence: 805]
He saw a massive jump in his intelligence.
It was all worth the torture, he thought, a smile tugging at his lips as he lay comfortably on the soft mattress and fell into a deep slumber as soon as his body touched the softness.
In the same endless expanse of grassy field.
No sunlight was there to wake him, yet he woke up on his own, rubbing his eyelids and stretching his arms.
Leon finally felt refreshed.
He didn’t know how long he had slept, but it was all worth it; he needed the rest.

He took out the cutlery, along with a steaming hot steak, soft, fluffy bread, a dish made from his potato and other ingredients, and some red wine, which didn’t make him feel drunk, but he still enjoyed the flavor.
He took each bite leisurely and savored every flavor.
Mmmh, so good!
If only enlightenment tasted half as good as steak.
He felt much more relaxed now.
He could see the path ahead, and the tension in his mind had lessened quite a bit.
This lunch, dinner, or breakfast—whatever it was—felt much more savory than before, even though it was the same food.
Yet it tasted different.
Storing everything inside his inventory with just a thought—fwoosh—as it all vanished.
He assumed a meditating position on the ground, his expression resolute as he began to study the first technique, Celestial White Moon Mana Formation Techniques.
As he processed the information, he started to understand why these techniques contained such a large amount of knowledge.
In addition to forming the mana heart, the technique explained how it was created.
Moon affinity was not an affinity in itself, but derived from the combination of different affinities.
Elements like
Water
Ice
Shadow
Illusion
And lastly, time.
These elements made up the core of Moon Affinity.
Five affinities for one power?
Who designed this system, a committee?
But water, the most basic affinity, took up the most significant part, reaching 45% of Moon Affinity.
Then ice: 20%.
Shadow: 15%.
Illusion: 15%.
Time: 5%.
This was the combination the founder of the Celestial White Moon Technique used to create her unique Moon affinity.
A blend of various affinities to make a unique one of her own.
The idea itself blew Leon’s mind completely away.
The founder’s words stated her technique was not perfect—no method was—as the limitation of affinity was always there, based on the five affinities she had and factoring in the rank of each one.
A harmony of balance between the affinities was the accumulation of her entire life.
An affinity of her own, which formed a single affinity that surpassed every affinity she had, breaking the power barrier imposed by affinity rank.

chapters.title: Chapter 177: Mana Heart Creation—Holy Energy Edition
paragraphs: Clearing away his previous thoughts, Leon’s expression was solemn as he could only use holy energy right now, and it was acting in such a way that no mana could be produced.
His throat felt dry, a faint chill crawling along his arms despite the golden light flickering at his fingertips.
This is really a big problem.
A dull ache settled behind his eyes, tension coiling at the base of his skull.
Just my luck—can’t get mana, but migraines are free.

He had to store the excess holy energy, and to do that, he had to make a mana heart. However, the way it was described, the completed rune needed to support the mana heart could only be made by moon affinity, as it was designed especially for it.
Let’s not lose hope now. First, I should finish learning about all the other techniques and see if there’s something that can help me.
One by one, Leon carefully went through each and every single one of the techniques.
Hours passed as his vision blurred, each page’s script swimming before his tired eyes, the air tinged with the musty scent of ancient parchment.
He focused entirely on something that could help his mana heart made out of holy energy.
One day had passed, and Leon hadn’t finished with all the techniques, but there was still nothing he had found that could help him as of now.
Every single rune was designed for a specific element or a combination of elements, creating a completely different affinity altogether.
He had thought the creator of the Celestial White Moon Mana Heart Formation was special. Still, all the rest of these techniques were equally special in their own unique way.

Sun affinity, blood affinity, star affinity, void affinity, charm affinity, and various others—each had its own distinctive combination and certain special conditions required to use. Still, all of them were powerful affinities, different from the norm.
A whole new, different world had been shown to him, which he had to explore later on.
One more day had passed. Leon still hadn’t found something completely concrete, but he had some ideas for now.
He was still not finished with a couple more techniques, so closing his eyes and giving his focus entirely to his mind, he continued.
The next day.
Leon’s eyes opened with a new, profound understanding in them.
Finally, I’ve found the way to use holy energy to create a mana core.
On the third day, after he began learning about the Heavenly Sword Mana Heart Formation techniques, all his doubts were cleared.
Besides the fact that he had learned different, unique things from other techniques, this technique was the very foundation of the way he was going to build his mana heart using holy energy.
This explained how people with no affinity or very low affinity could form a mana heart.
To form a mana heart, the thing you needed most was a very high level of control over the element that you were using as the core for your mana heart.
It was mentioned that after your mana heart is formed, a heavenly transformation would happen.
But I’m not sure if this would be the same for me or not, as I haven’t reached the Ethereal Lord stage yet. This transformation was supposed to happen then.
He didn’t even know how one reached the Ethereal Lord stage. Yet, he was directly jumping into creating a mana heart using his holy energy.
I have no choice. I have to do it. This holy energy will never let me use mana.
He clutched the red feather on his neck.
I have this for safety. At the very least, I won’t die.
A technique that uses pure holy energy to create the mana heart—he knew how different mana and holy energy were, yet they always tried to devour each other. He didn’t know what that even meant.
But he felt that this technique and rune—which was the most important for the method—were said to have been formed through the accumulation of knowledge and experiments spanning millions of years.

Especially this rune, created by the Heavenly Sword Demon Chun Ma, the very first of their kind. No previous knowledge like before, unlike other elements, where you could take inspiration from simpler elemental paths.
Chun Ma mentioned how hard it was to create his rune, as mana was the most raw form of element—much harder to grasp the meaning of something that could make everything.

Yet he did it in the end, from the passed-down knowledge from generations before him—those who had died without ever becoming immortal. He was the only successor who completed the wishes of every single one of his predecessors’ techniques.
It was not a technique created by him only, but by thousands of predecessors who died trying.

Leon had understood how precious the techniques were, yet they were given to him just like that, when the Guild Master of the Heavenly Sword had no obligation to. If he hadn’t sent him, Leon wouldn’t even have known it existed to begin with.

He didn’t understand the reason, so he focused on the process of starting to form his mana heart. And to do that, first, he needed better control over his holy energy, as it had to work in sync—one big mishap and he was done, and 2.5 million casualties, gone just like that.
Not just that—he also had to learn to create the rune outside so he didn’t blast himself from the inside.
This marked the beginning of Leon’s most arduous journey to master holy energy.
"IT’S BEEN THREE FUCKING MONTHS!"
His hands were raw, fingertips tingling from the endless attempts, while the muscles in his back and legs throbbed with every slight movement.
What did he learn to do during that time?
Practically nothing.
I could’ve learned to knit at this rate. At least scarves don’t explode.
If he compared this progress to any other element, it would be just a drop in the bucket for the whole three months.
I’m only able to control a single strand of holy energy with proper control. If I use more, this fucking holy energy acts like a man on crack whose personal air just got breathed in by a stranger.
Completely out of control.
I can use the strand of holy energy to create the whole heart, but it would take at least three years or even more.

That was also the amount of time he had left before the festival started. If he tried to be safe and first learned to create the primary rune replica outside of his body, he would not have nearly enough time.
Fuck it! Let’s do it directly...
His expression turned serious as he retook the meditation position, and a single strand of holy energy started moving toward his heart.
A tingling burn crawled through his veins, every nerve standing on edge as the shimmering strand spiraled closer to his heart.
